narrative.overview:
The hub reads as one author's book of works. It opens on a title page: the author's name set across the full measure at display scale, with "Works, since 2023" beneath it in the secondary ink. Below that come a thesis, a lede, a one-line colophon of countable facts, and a contents list of four chapters with roman numerals and work ranges. Next is an index of all thirty-six works, numbered No. 01–36. Then four chapters follow. Each chapter opens on a full-bleed cobalt page holding a huge roman numeral. After the opener, every work is presented as an architectural plate with a caption. The plate is the project's own pictogram redrawn in ink on a construction grid, framed by crop marks. Pictogram and caption are wrapped together in one link.

The register is daylight desk reading: cool light-grey paper, near-black ink, a secondary ink for captions, hairline rules, and a single cobalt. Hierarchy comes from scale, weight and position on a 12-column grid, never from ornament. There is one face, Schibsted Grotesk. It reaches from an 11.5rem title down to 0.875rem figure captions, using weights 400, 500 and 600 only. Depth is flat. The only colour field is the cobalt chapter opener. The only motion is one left-to-right plotter pass over each plate, the first time it enters the screen.

Density is that of a well-set book: generous margins, long vertical rests between works, and captions held to a reading measure. The index and contents exist so that a visitor can reach a work in one jump. The plates and captions let a reader linger.
keyCharacteristics: A book structure: title page, contents, index, chapters, plates, colophon.
Cool light-grey paper, two inks, one cobalt; no gradients, shadows or tints.
Schibsted Grotesk only, sentence case throughout, tight negative tracking at display sizes.
Plates are line drawings on a construction grid, with a strict three-weight stroke hierarchy.
A 12-column grid; three alternating plate/caption layouts.
Full-bleed cobalt chapter openers carrying a giant roman numeral.
One motion: the plotter pass, once per plate, absent under reduced motion and without JS.

rules.name: The One Cobalt Rule
rules.body: Cobalt is the only hue on the page. It appears as a full-bleed field in exactly one place, the chapter opener. Everywhere else it appears only as a *response*: hover, focus or selection. No resting text, rule or plate uses it.

rules.name: The Two Inks Rule
rules.body: Text is either ink or secondary ink, and nothing else. Meaning steps down by moving from ink to secondary ink, never by lowering opacity or lightening further.

rules.name: The Single Face Rule
rules.body: Schibsted Grotesk is the only typeface loaded. A new role is made by choosing a size and one of the weights 400/500/600, never by adding a family. CJK uses the system Han stack and is never given a webfont.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Nothing is uppercased or letter-spaced open. Labels, chapter titles and navigation are set in sentence case, at the size their role needs.

rules.name: The Tabular Number Rule
rules.body: Every work number, range and count uses tabular figures and two-digit numbering (01–36), so that columns of numbers align like a book's index.

rules.name: The Grid Rule
rules.body: Every element starts and ends on one of the 12 columns. Asymmetry is created by choosing columns, never by offsets or absolute positioning.

rules.name: The Touch Floor Rule
rules.body: Every interactive row or button is at least 44px tall, including index entries, language buttons and running-head links.

rules.name: The Printed Page Rule
rules.body: Nothing floats. If a surface needs separating, use a tonal step (paper → plate), a rule (hairline or ink) or a full colour field, in that order of preference.

rules.name: The Stroke Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: There are three line weights, never more: the object at 2.4px non-scaling, the crop marks at 0.75, and the grid, circle and dimensions at 0.5. A new plate redraws the project's real icon. It never uses a stock glyph, and never fills its grid with decoration.

dos: **Do** keep cobalt (#2340c8) as the single hue: full-bleed on chapter openers, and otherwise only as hover, focus and selection.
**Do** set every new role in Schibsted Grotesk at weight 400, 500 or 600, in sentence case.
**Do** number works with two tabular digits and keep the index, the contents ranges and the chapter count lines in agreement.
**Do** draw every new plate from the project's own 24-unit icon, scaled 7.5× into the 240 viewBox, with the object at 2.4px non-scaling stroke over the shared grid, crop marks and circle.
**Do** wrap each work's plate and caption in a single link, and place them on the 12-column grid using the A/B/C layouts in sequence.
**Do** write every visible string three times (`.en`, `.fr`, `.zh`) and let the body class decide which one shows.
**Do** keep interactive rows at least 44px tall and the focus ring a square 2px cobalt outline.
**Do** keep plates fully visible without JavaScript and under reduced motion; the plotter pass is an enhancement.
donts: **Don't** add a second typeface, a monospace face, or a webfont for CJK.
**Don't** introduce shadows, gradients, translucent overlays or rounded corners.
**Don't** add a second accent or per-project colours on the hub.
**Don't** uppercase or letter-space labels, or place small category labels (kickers) above headings; the one label on the page is the "Contents" heading of the contents list.
**Don't** use glyph or emoji arrows; arrows are authored SVG paths that inherit `currentColor`.
**Don't** add a fourth stroke weight to the plates or fill their grid with decoration.
**Don't** animate anything other than the plotter pass, and never replay it.
**Don't** add photographs, screenshots or raster images to the page.
